test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 31 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Acts ended the trade monopoly of the Company in India and opened it to all British subjects except tea?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Charter Act of 1813.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charter Act of 1813**

 
 
• **​**The Charter Act of 1813 was passed by the British Parliament.
 
• It renewed the East India Company’s charter for another 20 years.
 
• This is also called the **East India Company Act, 1813.**
 
• It defined for the first time the constitutional position of British Indian territories.
 
• This Act asserted the Crown’s sovereignty over British possessions in India.
 
• Their trade monopoly was ended except for the trade in tea, opium, and with China.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regulating Act, 1773**

 
 
• **​**The regulating Act of 1773 was passed by the British Parliament.
 
• It was passed to** control the territories of the East India Company** majorly in Bengal.
 
• This act permitted the company to retain its territorial possessions in India but sought to regulate the activities and functioning of the company.
 
• It did not take over power completely, hence called ‘regulating’.
 
 
 
• **Indian Council Act, 1861**
 
 
• **​**The Indian Councils Act 1861 was an act of the British Parliament.
 
• It made significant changes in the Governor-General’s Council. 
 
• It allowed for the decentralization of administration with the vesting of legislative power to the presidencies of Bombay and Madras.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
• **​**The Government of India Act was passed by the British Parliament in** August 1935.**
 
• It was the longest act enacted by the British Parliament at that time.
 
• It was divided into two separate acts namely
 
 
• the **Government of India Act 1935**
 
• the **Government of Burma Act 1935**
 
 
 
• Its aim was to make further provisions for the Government of India.
